title: Getting started with flowcam
text: NIMS requests work without key, unauthenticated traffic shares rate-limit pool across users. Register free key https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/signup/ store set_nims_key(): writes API_USGS_PAT ~/.Renviron applies current session immediately. Every subsequent call—session future R sessions—picks key automatically. dataRetrieval package reads environment variable, one key covers .
code: set_nims_key("your_api_key_here")

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: find_cameras() returns tibble camera metadata. Called arguments fetches every camera currently registered NIMS: Narrow specific USGS monitoring location passing NWIS site number: returns Pecos Web Camera near Roswell, NM. record reachable camera identifier: Key columns result: need couple fields—example scanning hundreds cameras—use return_fields keep response small: camId always returned regardless pass return_fields.
code: all_cameras <- find_cameras() nrow(all_cameras) cam <- find_cameras(site_id = "08385630") cam find_cameras(cam_id = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell") find_cameras(   site_id       = "08385630",   return_fields = c("camName", "newestImageDT", "TL_enabled") )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: list_images() returns filenames stored camera. Pass either cam_id site_id: default single-column tibble filenames ordered newest-first. Set raw_item = TRUE also retrieve capture timestamp file size: time argument accepts Date, POSIXct, ISO 8601 character value. single value means “”: two-element vector sets closed window. Use NA open bound: default results newest-first. Pass recent = FALSE flip order—useful want frames chronological order building animation: limit argument controls API page size (1–50,000). camera images limit, list_images() paginates automatically using timestamp cursor returns matching records single tibble.
code: imgs <- list_images("NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell", limit = 10) imgs list_images("NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell", limit = 10, raw_item = TRUE) list_images(   "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time = "2025-06-15" ) list_images(   "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time = c("2025-06-01", "2025-06-03") ) list_images("NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell", limit = 20, recent = FALSE)

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: time argument accepts Date, POSIXct, ISO 8601 character value. single value means “”: two-element vector sets closed window. Use NA open bound:
code: list_images(   "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time = "2025-06-15" ) list_images(   "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time = c("2025-06-01", "2025-06-03") )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: default results newest-first. Pass recent = FALSE flip order—useful want frames chronological order building animation:
code: list_images("NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell", limit = 20, recent = FALSE)

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: limit argument controls API page size (1–50,000). camera images limit, list_images() paginates automatically using timestamp cursor returns matching records single tibble.

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: download_images() lists images camera saves local directory one call. must create destination directory beforehand: paths character vector local file paths returned invisibly. Failed downloads represented NA. Pass time argument list_images() restrict images downloaded: download_images() skips files already exist dest_dir overwrite = FALSE (default). download interrupted, simply re-run call missing files fetched.
code: dest <- file.path(tempdir(), "roswell") dir.create(dest, showWarnings = FALSE)  paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   dest_dir = dest,   size     = "small",   limit    = 10 ) paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   dest_dir = dest,   size     = "small",   time     = c("2025-06-10", "2025-06-12") )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: Pass time argument list_images() restrict images downloaded:
code: paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   dest_dir = dest,   size     = "small",   time     = c("2025-06-10", "2025-06-12") )

text: download_images() skips files already exist dest_dir overwrite = FALSE (default). download interrupted, simply re-run call missing files fetched.

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: make_gif() fetches images encodes animated GIF. requires gifski package. simplest call streams images directly NIMS—separate download step needed: already downloaded images download_images(), point directory dir skip re-downloading: range spanning many days result can hundreds frames. Pass one_per_day = TRUE reduce animation single frame per calendar day, selecting image whose capture time closest local noon: output specified file written "<cam_id>.gif" working directory. 30-day example Pecos Web Camera near Roswell (one frame per day, closest noon):  Pecos Web Camera near Roswell — April 6 May 5, 2026
code: make_gif(   cam_id = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time   = c("2025-06-10", "2025-06-12"),   fps    = 2,   output = "roswell.gif" ) make_gif(   dir    = dest,   fps    = 2,   output = "roswell.gif" ) make_gif(   cam_id      = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time        = c("2025-05-01", "2025-06-30"),   fps         = 4,   one_per_day = TRUE,   output      = "roswell_monthly.gif" )

code: make_gif(   cam_id      = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time        = c("2025-05-01", "2025-06-30"),   fps         = 4,   one_per_day = TRUE,   output      = "roswell_monthly.gif" )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: make_video() produces MP4 instead GIF. requires av package accepts arguments make_gif(): Build already-downloaded directory: MP4 files substantially smaller equivalent GIFs resolution frame count, making preferable longer time ranges larger image sizes. GIFs portable sharing contexts don’t support video embedding.
code: make_video(   cam_id = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time   = c("2025-06-10", "2025-06-12"),   fps    = 4,   output = "roswell.mp4" ) make_video(   dir    = dest,   fps    = 4,   output = "roswell.mp4" )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: vignette("pecos-river") shows use find_gage_cameras() enrich camera records NWIS site metadata compare two cameras river reach. full function reference https://connorb.github.io/flowcam/reference/.

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: find_gage_cameras() wraps find_cameras() joins NWIS site attributes—drainage area, state, county, hydrologic unit code—via dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_monitoring_location(). result every column returned find_cameras() plus enriched NWIS columns available. Columns added NWIS join include: Compare drainage area two sites—Acme downstream contributing watershed larger: Check image availability downloading. newestImageDT (UTC) tells camera last reported:
code: roswell <- find_gage_cameras("08385630") roswell acme <- find_gage_cameras("08386000") acme data.frame(   site      = c("Roswell", "Acme"),   site_id   = c("08385630", "08386000"),   drain_mi2 = c(roswell$drain_area_va, acme$drain_area_va),   lat       = c(roswell$lat, acme$lat),   lng       = c(roswell$lng, acme$lng) ) roswell$newestImageDT acme$newestImageDT

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: Use time window sites image sets directly comparable. two-element vector passed time sets closed interval; single value means “”: Bind two results compare counts timestamps side side: raw_item = TRUE returns camId, filename, timestamp, fs (file size kilobytes). timestamps UTC strings NIMS format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ).
code: window <- c("2025-06-10", "2025-06-13")  roswell_imgs <- list_images(   "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time     = window,   raw_item = TRUE,   recent   = FALSE        # chronological order )  acme_imgs <- list_images(   "NM_Pecos_River_near_Acme",   time     = window,   raw_item = TRUE,   recent   = FALSE ) rbind(   cbind(site = "Roswell (08385630)", roswell_imgs),   cbind(site = "Acme (08386000)",    acme_imgs) )

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: Create separate destination directory site files don’t mix: Download Roswell images first: Acme images: calls skip files already exist disk (overwrite = FALSE default), re-running interrupted download safe. Switch size = "overlay" want full-resolution images gage-height annotation overlaid.
code: roswell_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "roswell") acme_dir    <- file.path(tempdir(), "acme") dir.create(roswell_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create(acme_dir,    showWarnings = FALSE) roswell_paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   dest_dir = roswell_dir,   size     = "small",   time     = window ) acme_paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = "NM_Pecos_River_near_Acme",   dest_dir = acme_dir,   size     = "small",   time     = window )

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: Build animated GIF images already disk pointing dir download directory. avoids second round network requests: time range spanning multiple days, one_per_day = TRUE reduces animation one frame per calendar day—image captured closest local noon camera’s time zone. keeps GIF becoming unwieldy long monitoring period: Adjust fps control playback speed: 1–2 fps gives enough time read individual frames flood event; 4+ fps better seasonal overview want convey change weeks. make_gif() requires gifski package (jpeg/png JPEG-format source images, NIMS typically serves). 30-day example Roswell camera (one frame per day):  Pecos Web Camera near Roswell — April 6 May 5, 2026
code: make_gif(   dir    = roswell_dir,   fps    = 3,   output = "roswell_event.gif" ) make_gif(   cam_id      = "NM_Pecos_Web_Camera_near_Roswell",   time        = c("2025-05-01", "2025-06-30"),   fps         = 4,   one_per_day = TRUE,   output      = "roswell_seasonal.gif" )

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: make_video() produces MP4 inputs. accepts identical arguments make_gif() requires av package: can also stream directly NIMS without prior download: MP4 resolution frame count substantially smaller GIF. multi-day event hundreds frames, video generally better choice; GIF convenient embedding tools don’t support video. 30-day window Acme camera comparison:  Pecos River near Acme — April 6 May 5, 2026
code: make_video(   dir    = acme_dir,   fps    = 3,   output = "acme_event.mp4" ) make_video(   cam_id = "NM_Pecos_River_near_Acme",   time   = window,   fps    = 3,   output = "acme_event.mp4" )

title: Comparing two Pecos River gages with flowcam
text: Check newestImageDT first. timestamp hours days old camera may offline. Spot-check committing large download. Use "thumb" exploration. Thumbnails around 200 px tall much smaller "small" images. Download thumb set first verify coverage switching "small" "overlay". Time zones. NIMS timestamps UTC. tz column camera metadata records camera’s local IANA time zone need convert display one_per_day interpretation. Large downloads. "small" images roughly 150–300 KB . 30-day window one image per 15 minutes around 2,900 files (~600 MB). Plan accordingly use overwrite = FALSE resume safely. Rate limits. Unauthenticated requests share pool across users. Store API key set_nims_key() (see vignette("getting-started")) use personal allocation. Full function reference: https://connorb.github.io/flowcam/reference/

title: Access USGS Stream Gage Camera Images via the NIMS API
code: library(flowcam)  # Store your free USGS API key (one-time setup) set_nims_key("your_api_key_here")  # Find the camera at the Kansas River at Wamego, KS cam <- find_cameras(site_id = "06887500")  # List the 20 most recent images with timestamps list_images(cam$camId, limit = 20, raw_item = TRUE)  # Download the last 30 days of images dest <- file.path(tempdir(), "kaw") dir.create(dest)  date_range <- c(Sys.Date() - 30, Sys.Date())  download_images(   cam_id   = cam$camId,   dest_dir = dest,   size     = "small",   time     = date_range )  # Assemble into an animated GIF (one frame per day, 10 fps) make_gif(dir = dest, fps = 10, one_per_day = TRUE, output = "kaw.gif")  # Or an MP4 video make_video(dir = dest, fps = 10, one_per_day = TRUE, output = "kaw.mp4")

title: List image filenames for a NIMS camera — list_images
text: cam_id Character. Camera identifier. Use find_cameras() look valid IDs. used together site_id. limit Integer 1 50000. Number records fetched per API request (page size). Default 1000. matching images returned via automatic pagination regardless value. recent Logical. TRUE (default), return recent images first. FALSE, return oldest images first. time POSIXct, Date, character vector length 1 2 used filter images capture time. length-1 value treated start (). length-2 vector sets start end; use NA open bound (c("2025-06-01", NA) = ; c(NA, "2025-06-02") = ). Character strings passed unchanged; API accepts ISO 8601 ("2025-12-31T00:00:00") NIMS format ("2025-12-31T00-00-00Z"). raw_item Logical. TRUE, return tibble columns camId, filename, timestamp, fs (file size kb). FALSE (default), return single-column tibble filenames. site_id Character. NWIS site number (e.g. "05366800" "USGS-05366800"). used together cam_id. site one camera, supply cam_id directly.
